_comment: The products OIO actually sells. A design is artwork; a product is that artwork on one blank we chose. `primary` is the one card that represents a design inside its category — the rest surface through 'Also on' on the product page.
_scope: T-shirts only, one product per design: a single Bella + Canvas Unisex Jersey (175) tee, chosen for its tall, well-cut, non-boxy fit. The customer picks colour then size inside the design. Bella comes in exactly seven colours (white, black, navy, red, olive, slate, heather gray) and the blank carries no others — the fuller palettes on Spreadshirt belong to boxy or men's-cut shirts, so the seven are the price of the good cut and the line accepts them. Two designs step off Bella by necessity: Save the Stick - Bones prints white and needs the Gildan Heavyweight (1361) for a light ink, and Datsun Honey Bee needs sun yellow and runs on the Premium cut (812 men's / 813 women's). Honey Bee is also the only design with a second cut; everything else is the one unisex tee.

5d89f19b162c5f464e875bc1._why: Datsun Honey Bee — the one design that can't be Bella: its badge is designed for a sun-yellow ground and no unisex blank carries yellow. Stays on the Premium cut, sold as a men's (812) and women's (813) pair, both sun yellow. A tank was considered and dropped — no tank on Spreadshirt comes in yellow, and the badge dies on any other ground.

_curation: Colourways are Ian's call design by design, made against rendered contact sheets. `appearanceIds` on a byDesign entry is the allowlist of garment colours that survive; anything not listed is off the shelf.
